reasoning: Both attempts implement the task and validate remote arguments safely. B is tidier, has slightly better comments and passes stylua, which A fails. But A's guard on blocksOf[player] stops a PlaceBlock that is processed after PlayerRemoving from creating a block nobody owns. B misses that case, so its leave cleanup isn't airtight and per-player state can leak. A formatting failure is fixed by running the formatter. A correctness gap like B's is easy to miss in review, so A wins narrowly.

criteria.note: It creates both remotes and the PlacedBlocks folder, validates through PlacementRules.validate, enforces the cap and the os.clock cooldown, and keeps blocksOf/blockCount in step through removeBlock; the `if not owned then return` guard also stops a placement arriving after PlayerRemoving from leaving an orphaned block.
RemoveBlock checks typeof Instance and IsA BasePart, then requires ownerOf[target] == player before destroying; PlaceBlock passes the unknown arguments straight to validate.
The comment saying the OwnerUserId attribute is never trusted carries a real constraint; '-- Player is leaving (or hasn't been registered yet)' explains the guard, though it reads close to narration.
Comments are few and placed next to their code; the two-line ownership comment could fit on one line.
No change history and no references to the request.
It reuses BlockTypes.STYLES and PlacementRules.BLOCK_SIZE, uses --!strict and passes luau-lsp and selene, but fails stylua on the long Connect line.

Remotes, folder, validation, cap and cooldown are all correct, but it has no registered-player guard: a PlaceBlock processed after PlayerRemoving creates a block that never gets removed and re-adds a blockCounts entry for the departed player.
`typeof(block) ~= "Instance" or ownerByBlock[block] ~= player` ensures only a server-created block owned by the sender is destroyed, and it also re-checks that `result` is a Vector3.
Both comments justify things the code can't show: why the table is keyed by Instance, and why the BlockType cast is safe.
Two single-line comments, each next to the line it governs.
It reuses BlockTypes and PlacementRules, is a clean set of named handlers, and passes luau-lsp, selene and stylua.

strengths: Guards against a placement that arrives after the player has left
Per-player owned sets make cleanup on leave O(owned)
Thorough check on the RemoveBlock argument
weaknesses: Keeps three parallel tables of per-player state, which is slightly redundant
A placement in flight when the player leaves leaves a permanent orphaned block and a leaked count entry
PlayerRemoving scans every placed block in the server
